### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** The period 1820–1850 encompasses War of 1812 veterans (service 1812–1815) who would have been alive and filing pension claims throughout; the Mexican-American War (1846–1848) produced service records and bounty land warrants for Berkshire County men
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, and bounty land warrants at the National Archives (NARA); state adjutant general records at the Massachusetts Archives
- **Where held:** NARA (https://www.archives.gov/) holds federal military records. Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) has digitized War of 1812 service records and pension index cards. The Massachusetts Archives holds state militia and muster rolls

### Cemetery records

- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave (https://www.findagrave.com/) holds transcribed and photographed entries for many Berkshire County cemeteries; coverage is volunteer-driven and incomplete
- **Physical records:** Town sexton records and burial-ground registers are held by individual town clerks or local historical societies in Berkshire County

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The Berkshire area had active local papers by the 1820s. The specific titles and date ranges were not confirmed by a Berkshire-specific wiki page in this survey
- **Where held:** Newspapers.com (https://www.newspapers.com/) and digitized collections at the Massachusetts Digital Commonwealth (https://www.digitalcommonwealth.org/) hold historical Massachusetts newspapers; check both for Berkshire County papers
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, and legal notices (estate advertisements, land sale notices) are valuable supplements to thin vital records

### Immigration / emigration records

- **Context:** Berkshire County is an inland county with no port of entry. Immigrants arriving at Boston or New York City and moving inland to Berkshire County are the typical immigration pattern for this period
- **Relevant ports:** Boston, MA; New York City, NY
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival lists (pre-1891 these are ship manifests); declarations of intention and naturalization petitions filed at Berkshire County or state courts; alien registrations
- **FamilySearch collections:** "Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820-1891" (id: 1784312; https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1784312) covers the period, though Berkshire County residents arriving via Boston would be represented here. "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790-1906" (id: 1459213; https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1459213) covers naturalizations filed in Massachusetts courts
- **Important note:** Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in any court of record — county court, state court, or federal court — not just the federal court. Search Berkshire County court records as well as NARA for naturalization petitions

### Tax records

- **Types:** Town property valuation lists (annual, by town) and county tax records
- **Date range:** Town-level tax lists in Massachusetts predate this period and run continuously through it
- **Where held:** Individual town clerks and the Massachusetts Archives. These are largely not digitized
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists name heads of household and can substitute for missing census years or confirm residence

### Other record types

- **Town meeting records:** Each town kept its own meeting records — these name residents receiving assistance, holding office, or involved in town business, and can supplement thin vital records
- **School records:** Town-level school committee records may survive at individual town archives or the Massachusetts Archives

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

## Records NOT online

- Town clerk original vital record volumes (the two FamilySearch digitized volumes are browse-only, not name-indexed; most individual town clerk volumes remain physical-only)
- County court minute books and common pleas records
- Town tax valuation lists (the large bulk of these are not digitized)
- Town meeting records
- Most denominational church registers other than the Pittsfield Congregational volume on FamilySearch
- School committee records

## Known record losses

No tool result in this survey states that specific Berkshire County record sets were destroyed or lost. The absence of a larger set of digitized volumes reflects a digitization gap, not necessarily loss. For confirmed survival or loss of specific record sets, contact the Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, the Probate Court, and the Massachusetts Archives directly.

## Research tips

- **Town, not county, is the vital records unit.** For 1820–1840, Massachusetts had no statewide registration system; the event was recorded only in the town where it occurred. Know your subject's town of residence before searching, and remember that marriage intentions may be in the bride's town, the groom's town, or both. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records)
- **Use the published "Vital Records to 1850" series first.** Over 200 Massachusetts town volumes have been published as transcriptions, and they cover Berkshire County towns. These are compiled abstracts, so verify any entry against the original town clerk record when possible. Source: Massachusetts Genealogy article, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial
- **The two FamilySearch Berkshire volumes must be browsed image by image.** The town clerk vital records volume (image group 004500891, 512 images) and the Pittsfield Congregational Church volume (image group 004500892, 274 images) are neither name-indexed nor full-text searchable. Plan for a systematic browse of both volumes for a family in Pittsfield.
- **The 1850 census is a turning point.** The 1820, 1830, and 1840 federal censuses name only the head of household; the 1850 census names every person. If your family appears in the 1850 census with children who were born 1820–1849, their ages will help reconstruct births that may be missing from vital records.
- **Search across both state lines.** A family near the New York or Vermont borders very likely generated records on both sides. Columbia County and Rensselaer County (New York, to the west) and Bennington County (Vermont, to the north) each had their own vital registration systems, church registers, land deeds, and probate courts. New York did not have statewide vital registration until after this period; Vermont recorded vital events at the town level. Search the adjoining county deed and probate records as well as the Massachusetts ones, particularly if the family owned land or had relatives on the other side. The specific neighboring towns within those counties were not listed in a Berkshire County wiki table in this survey; ask the Berkshire County Historical Society or consult a detailed Berkshire County town map.
- **NEHGS is the essential regional complement to FamilySearch.** The New England Historic Genealogical Society (americanancestors.org) holds transcribed vital records, church records, and manuscript collections that fill gaps in the FamilySearch digitized holdings for western Massachusetts. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial

**Note on FamilySearch Wiki coverage:** The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Massachusetts (home overview, getting started, online records, research tips) and for Massachusetts-specific record types (Church Records, Land and Property, Probate Records, Census, Naming Customs) all returned only generic content in this survey rather than the Massachusetts-specific articles. The specific Massachusetts pages likely exist but could not be fetched during this survey run. Consult them directly at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy before finalizing your research plan.

---

Berkshire County, Massachusetts sits in the far western corner of the state, touching New York on one side and Vermont on the other, and for the years 1820 to 1850 it offers a solid but scattered set of records. The most important thing to know is that until 1841 there was no statewide registry: births, marriages, and deaths were recorded town by town, and you have to know which of Berkshire's towns your family lived in before you can find those records. From 1841 onward the state began collecting copies from each town, so the records become easier to track down. Church baptism registers are essential for filling in pre-1841 births, and many Berkshire town registers have been transcribed in published "Vital Records to 1850" volumes held at libraries and genealogical societies. FamilySearch has digitized two Berkshire County volumes, but both must be browsed page by page with no name search — plan for that. For census years falling in the period, the 1820, 1830, and 1840 federal censuses name only the head of household, while the 1850 census names everyone, making it the single most useful snapshot for the whole family.

The next step is to identify the specific Berkshire County town your family lived in, then search the published vital records transcriptions and the FamilySearch town clerk volume for that town, and check church records for any denomination represented in that town — after which a research plan can map out the census, probate, and cross-border records in a logical sequence.

### Research Tips: Naming Conventions

*(This is the only section with confirmed tool data — sourced from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs)*

- Irish surnames bearing the prefixes **Mac** (son of) and **O** (grandson/descendant of) were frequently dropped or restored over time. The same family may appear as, e.g., O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn across different records — search all forms.
- **Spelling was not standardized.** A single family's surname may appear in several different spellings within one parish.

- Some given names were used for **both males and females** (Florence, Sydney, Evelyn are wiki examples).
- A **traditional naming pattern** was used by Irish parents into the later 19th century:

  | Child | Named for |
  |---|---|
  | 1st son | Father's father |
  | 2nd son | Mother's father |
  | 3rd son | Father |
  | 4th son | Father's eldest brother |
  | 1st daughter | Mother's mother |
  | 2nd daughter | Father's mother |
  | 3rd daughter | Mother |

- **Important:** The naming pattern is a clue, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity.

## Research tips

**Naming conventions** — the one section with confirmed tool data, sourced from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Naming_Customs:

- Irish surnames bearing the prefixes *Mac* (son of) and *O* (grandson or descendant of) became fixed parts of hereditary surnames and were frequently dropped or restored over time. The same family may appear as, for example, O'Flynn, Flynn, and Flinn across different records — search all forms.
- Spelling was not standardized; a single family's surname may be recorded in several different ways in one parish.
- Many Irish surnames and given names were anglicized under English rule, producing multiple variant forms. Darby, Dermot, and Jeremiah are all anglicizations of the same Irish given name. The same process applies to surnames: Houlihan or O'Houlihan may appear as Holland.
- Some given names were used for both males and females — Florence, Sydney, and Evelyn are examples from the wiki page.
- Some given names have nicknames that bear little resemblance to the formal name.
- A traditional naming pattern was used by Irish parents until the later nineteenth century (from the same page):
  - First son: usually named for the father's father
  - Second son: usually named for the mother's father
  - Third son: usually named for the father
  - Fourth son: usually named for the father's eldest brother
  - First daughter: usually named for the mother's mother
  - Second daughter: usually named for the father's mother
  - Third daughter: usually named for the mother
- The naming pattern is a clue, not a rule — it was not universally followed, and a broken pattern is not evidence of non-identity (from the same page).

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 (from place_search dateRange +1811/)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed by tool results during this survey
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** Not available — the population tool returned no data for this place during this survey
- **Economy:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by tool results; church records volume (image group 007936751) covers 1842–1895 in both English and German, indicating German-speaking congregations were present alongside English-speaking ones
- **Religious denominations:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by tool results

**Note on FamilySearch Wiki coverage:** All four wiki place-page sections (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips) and all specific Pennsylvania record-type pages requested (Vital Records, Land and Property, Church Records, Probate Records, Census, Naming Customs) returned only generic fallback content rather than Pennsylvania- or Schuylkill County-specific pages. Facts that would normally come from those pages are noted as unconfirmed throughout this guide. Consult the FamilySearch Wiki directly — especially https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Schuylkill_County,_Pennsylvania_Genealogy — before treating any such absence as definitive.

## Boundary changes
- Schuylkill County was formed in 1811, per the standard place record (dateRange +1811/). No boundary changes during 1840–1880 were identified in tool results during this survey.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** No specific start date or registration level was returned by the FamilySearch Wiki during this survey — the Pennsylvania Vital Records page returned only generic content. Consult that page directly for the registration level and year.
- **What exists:** One digitized volume of Marriage Records (1870–1910, image group 007936753, 94 images) overlaps the target period. This volume is 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — it must be browsed image-by-image.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (browse-only); originals at the county level
- **Gaps:** No birth or death volumes were identified for the target period in this survey. Marriage records within this volume begin at 1870.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (see below); newspapers; cemetery records; family bibles

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Not confirmed by tool results; image group 007936751 is in both English and German, indicating English- and German-speaking congregations
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials (typical for the period)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds one digitized volume (image group 007936751, 187 images, 1842–1895). A collection titled "Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)" (collection SYNTH-PA-CHURCH, 1708–1985, 982,415 persons, 1,245,830 records) also appears in collections_search — its title includes the phrase "synthetic test fixture," indicating it may be a demo or test entry; verify its status at FamilySearch before relying on it as a live research collection.
- **Gaps:** The digitized volume (007936751) is 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — browse image-by-image. Coverage begins at 1842.
- **Language:** Records in the digitized volume are in both English and German. Researchers must be able to read German for German-language entries.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** The 1850 United States Federal Census for Schuylkill County is accessible and indexed on Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/). Federal decennial censuses were taken for 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 within the target period.
- **State/provincial census:** No Pennsylvania state census volumes were identified in this survey.
- **Other enumerations:** Mortality schedules (which typically accompanied federal censuses 1850–1880) were not separately identified for Schuylkill County in this survey; check the FamilySearch Catalog.
- **Access:** The 1850 federal census for Schuylkill County is indexed on Ancestry. No census volumes appeared in the FamilySearch digitized volume results for this county and period.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, administrations, inventories, guardianships
- **Date range:** 1851–1930 (image group 007936749); collection 1999196 covers 1683–1994
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds one browse-only digitized volume of probate records (image group 007936749, 412 images, 1851–1930; 0% indexed). Additionally, collection "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" (collection 1999196) has 3,200,560 images and covers 1683–1994, though it has 0 name-indexed records — browse-only.
- **Access level:** Browse-only images for both; must be browsed image-by-image

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Not confirmed by tool results (the Pennsylvania Land and Property wiki page returned generic content)
- **Types:** Deeds
- **Date range:** 1815–1900 (image group 007936752)
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds one digitized volume of Deed Records (image group 007936752, 543 images, 1815–1900). This is the only partially indexed volume among all five for Schuylkill County — 22% name-indexed. The remaining 78% must be browsed.
- **Tax records:** Ancestry curates "Pennsylvania, U.S., Tax and Exoneration Lists, 1768–1801" (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/), which predates the 1840 target period but may provide earlier family property context.

### Military records
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, draft registrations
- **Where held:** National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). No Schuylkill County–specific military volumes were identified in the volume_search results.
- **Access:** Military records at NARA are accessible in person and through online databases including FamilySearch and Ancestry.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Online coverage:** No FindAGrave, BillionGraves, or other cemetery index results were returned in the external_links_search results for this place and period
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers — no specific holdings confirmed by tool results

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Where held:** Not confirmed by tool results
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage and death notices, legal notices (typical value for this period and place)

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Not specifically confirmed by tool results for this county
- **Record types:** Naturalization records; passenger lists at NARA; alien registrations
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds one browse-only digitized volume of Naturalization Records (image group 007936750, 298 images, 1849–1915; 0% indexed). Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in any court of record.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members — children as young as newborns are listed.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Tax and exoneration lists
- **Date range:** 1768–1801 available via Ancestry (predates target period)
- **Where held:** Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/)
- **Substitute value:** Pre-period tax records can help establish earlier family presence and property holdings before the 1840–1880 window

### Other record types
- Court minute books, guardianship files, and other county court records are not separately confirmed in this survey — check the Schuylkill County Courthouse and Pennsylvania State Archives.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Gap it fills | Access |

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, County Antrim, province of Ulster
- **Towns within the parish:** Bushmills and Dervock (the user named Bushmills as the area of interest)
- **Parent jurisdiction during 1780–1870:** Part of Ireland within the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland (from 1801 under the Act of Union); from 1922 this area became part of Northern Ireland, remaining in the United Kingdom. The FamilySearch Wiki confirms that County Antrim is one of the six Ulster counties that voted to remain in the United Kingdom in 1922. ([Ireland Church Records, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Religious composition:** Per the FamilySearch Wiki, in Northern Ireland (which includes County Antrim) the Church of Ireland and Presbyterian churches together accounted for approximately 60 percent of the population in 1861; Catholics accounted for approximately 40 percent. The Bushmills/north Antrim area had a particularly strong Church of Ireland and Presbyterian character due to the 17th-century Ulster plantation from Scotland. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Ecclesiastical jurisdiction:** This survey did not confirm the specific diocese for Billy parish from tool results. The researcher should consult the PRONI Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf), which the FamilySearch Wiki specifically names as identifying "what churches exist in each parish, what records exist for each church and whether the records are available in PRONI." ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Key historical event:** The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin destroyed a large portion of Ireland's centrally held records, including approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers that had been deposited there. This is the defining event for Irish genealogical research and shapes every record class below. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

## Boundary changes

County Antrim was a stable jurisdiction throughout 1780–1870. No boundary change affected the civil parish of Billy during this period. The major administrative shift occurred in 1921–1922 when Ireland was partitioned: County Antrim joined Northern Ireland. As a result, records created before 1922 may be held at either PRONI in Belfast (Northern Ireland's archive) or at the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin, depending on record type and original custodian. The FamilySearch Wiki notes that "copies of many national records up to 1922 are available in both the NAI and PRONI." ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** Civil registration in Ireland began in 1864, confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki. The page states explicitly: "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) This means that 84 of the 90 years in the 1780–1870 target window fall entirely outside civil registration. Only the years 1864–1870 are covered by civil records for births and deaths.
- **What exists for 1864–1870:** Births, marriages, and deaths registered at the district registrar level. For Northern Ireland, civil registration records are held at the General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI). The FamilySearch Wiki notes that for Northern Ireland, civil registration is under GRONI, separate from the GRO in Dublin. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Pre-registration alternatives (1780–1864):** Church records are the only systematic vital-event records for this window. See Church records section below.
- **Access:** Civil registration records for 1864–1870 for County Antrim are held at GRONI. PRONI also holds indexed copies. This survey did not confirm whether these years are online.

### Church records

This is the central record class for the entire 1780–1870 window and demands the most detailed treatment.

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopalian)**

- The FamilySearch Wiki states that Church of Ireland records began in 1536 and that the denomination served as "the religion of many of the Northern Ireland London Company plantation settlers in the 17th century." Two-thirds of deposited Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- For parishes in County Antrim (Northern Ireland), surviving registers that were not destroyed in 1922 are held at PRONI in Belfast. The RCB Library in Dublin (Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14; library@ireland.anglican.org) holds the remaining Church of Ireland registers not at PRONI, and publishes a List of Parish Registers (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) showing which registers survive and where they are held. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **To determine whether Billy parish Church of Ireland registers survive and what their date range is:** Consult (1) the RCB Library list above, (2) the PRONI Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf), and (3) PRONI's list of digitised church records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni). All three are confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Online access — Church of Ireland registers:** The Ffolliott Collection at FindMyPast (https://search.findmypast.com) holds indexed extracts of Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Marriages, and Burials for many Church of Ireland parishes, including from County Antrim. - **Marriage bonds:** The FamilySearch collection [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) covers diocesan bonds including those from County Antrim's diocese for the full target period.   ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

**Presbyterian**

- The FamilySearch Wiki states that in 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled predominantly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to Ulster, and that "numerous registers date from the 1600s, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." Given the strong Scottish Presbyterian settlement of north County Antrim, Presbyterian registers for Bushmills-area congregations may begin earlier than the 1830 average. For the rural north Antrim area, Catholic registers for Billy parish may begin around 1828–1835, though earlier entries are possible. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Online access:** The National Library of Ireland hosts Catholic parish registers at https://registers.nli.ie/ — the primary free online source for Catholic records. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

For Billy civil parish, this is the fastest way to establish whether Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic registers survive and what years they cover. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

2. **Search Church of Ireland records even if the family was not Church of Ireland.** The FamilySearch Wiki advises: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." Before 1845, CoI churches performed many non-CoI marriages because only their ceremonies were legally recognized. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

3. **Search Catholic records even though they begin late.** Catholic rural registers in Ulster often begin around 1828 (after Catholic Emancipation). Earlier Catholic baptisms and marriages may be unrecorded or recorded only in CoI registers. The National Library of Ireland at registers.nli.ie is free and should be searched first for Catholic records. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

5. **Use the Ulster Historical Foundation** (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) for County Antrim research. The FamilySearch Wiki specifically names it as a large database covering Ulster. ([Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

6. **Search the FamilySearch Catalog directly** at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog using "Antrim, Ireland" as the place. This survey's automated catalog tools returned no results for Irish places; the catalog itself is known to hold extensive County Antrim microfilm, which must be browsed directly.

---

*This guide was built from confirmed tool results. The only substantive-content specific tool result was the FamilySearch Wiki page at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records. All place-resolution tools (place_search, collections_search, volume_search) and most wiki_read calls returned no results or only generic content for Irish places. Claims derived from that one source are cited inline; all other record types note that specific tool confirmation was not available. Re-running this guide with improved Ireland tool coverage may surface additional collections.*

---

For researchers of Billy civil parish, County Antrim in the 1780–1870 period: the records that survive are almost entirely church registers (Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic), held primarily at the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland in Belfast, with surviving Church of Ireland registers also potentially at the Representative Church Body Library in Dublin. Civil registration only begins in 1864, so the first 84 years of your window depend entirely on church records. The single most important warning is the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin, which destroyed roughly two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers that had been deposited there — before spending time on a CoI search, check the PRONI Guide to Church Records to confirm whether the specific Billy parish register survived and where it is held today.

The next step is to consult the PRONI Guide to Church Records online to confirm which Billy/Bushmills-area registers exist for each denomination, then to search the FamilySearch Catalog at https://www.familysearch.org/search/catalog for County Antrim microfilm holdings, and to run a research plan covering the specific register series confirmed to survive.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Location:** Partly in barony of Carey, chiefly Lower Dunluce; post town: Bushmills; Poor Law Union: Coleraine.
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland (archdeaconry of Connor), Presbyterian, Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian), and Wesleyan Methodist.
- **Important note:** For Roman Catholic records, Billy falls under the **RC district of Coleraine**, Diocese of Connor — Catholic vital-event entries for Billy residents appear under "Coleraine" in every index and repository, not under "Billy."

---

## Civil Registration

- **Births & deaths:** State registration began **1864** only — no civil records exist before that year anywhere in Ireland.
- **Marriages:** Protestant marriages registered from **1845**; all marriages from **1864**.
- **Custodian:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Belfast, and General Register Office of Ireland, Dublin (pre-partition copies).
- **Gap:** The years 1780–1863 have no civil birth/death registration. For 1780–1844, no civil marriage records exist either. Church registers are the only official source for the bulk of this window.

---

## Church Records & Gap-Closing Resources

### Presbyterian

| Coverage | FamilySearch Volume | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Christenings 1837–1868 (Ballylinny congregation) | Image group 007907410 | Free at FamilySearch.org — **full-text searchable**, not name-indexed |
| Marriages 1837–1864 | Image group 007765074 | Free at FamilySearch.org — **full-text searchable**, not name-indexed |

**Gap 1780–1836:** No Presbyterian register coverage confirmed for this sub-period.

Gap-closing repositories:
- **PRONI** (microfilm of surviving registers): 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast BT3 9HQ; proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; PRONI Guide to Church Records: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf
- **FindMyPast Non-Conformist Collections** (subscription): http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms (and parallel pages for marriages, burials, congregational records)

### Church of Ireland

No specific register start dates confirmed for Billy CoI by this survey. Two-thirds of Irish CoI registers deposited in Dublin were destroyed in the **1922 Public Record Office fire**.

Gap-closing repositories:
- **PRONI** (Belfast) — check the Guide to Church Records first to determine whether Billy's registers survived and in what form.
- **Representative Church Body (RCB) Library**, Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14 D14 N735; library@ireland.anglican.org; genealogy request service: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy; full register list: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
- **FamilySearch — Marriage License Bonds, 1623–1866** (Connor diocese included): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239 — free; important pre-civil-registration substitute.
- **FindMyPast** — Ffolliott CoI collections (baptisms, marriages, burials) and Betham/Thrift genealogical abstracts (subscription substitutes for destroyed originals): https://www.findmypast.com

### Roman Catholic (Coleraine district, Diocese of Connor)

Rural Catholic registers typically did not begin until after Catholic Emancipation (1828–1829). No pre-1864 registers are confirmed for the Coleraine district by this survey.

**Gap 1780–c.1828:** Entirely absent; no Catholic registers survive.  
**Gap c.1829–1863:** Sparse and unconfirmed start date for Coleraine.

Gap-closing repositories:
- **National Library of Ireland Catholic Registers** — free digitised collection: https://registers.nli.ie/
- **Ancestry** — Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 (collection 61039), subscription: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/
- **RootsIreland** (indexed Ulster church records, subscription): http://www.rootsireland.ie/
- **Ulster Historical Foundation** (subscription): http://www.ancestryireland.com/
- **PRONI** (Belfast) — holds microfilm of some Coleraine Catholic registers.

### Wesleyan Methodist & Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian)

No register dates confirmed for either denomination in Billy parish. Use the **PRONI Guide to Church Records** (URL above) as the first step, then FindMyPast Non-Conformist Congregational Records: http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records

---

## Census Records

Irish census records for 1821–1861 were largely destroyed in the 1922 fire (the 1861 and 1871 originals had been destroyed earlier by government order). The 1901 and 1911 censuses (post-period) are free at https://www.nationalarchives.ie/.

**Substitutes for the target period:**
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s):** Names landholders by townland; free at AskAboutIreland.ie and partially on Ancestry.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848–1864):** Names all property occupiers. Fully indexed and free at http://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/. A browse-only FamilySearch volume also exists for the townland of Ballylinny (image group 004689599, 76 images).

---

## Land, Tax & Probate Records

- **Registry of Deeds, Dublin** — land transactions from 1708.
- **Estate papers** at PRONI — leases and rent rolls for County Antrim tenant families.
- **Pre-1858 probate:** Original wills destroyed in 1922. Surviving indexes at Ancestry (collection 62077, free index): https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/; and abstracts via Betham/Thrift collections at FindMyPast.
- **Post-1858 probate:** PRONI holds County Antrim probate calendars.

---

## School Records

- **Deffrick National School Girls' Register** (image group 008682995), April 1867–September 1933: 50 images, browse-only at FamilySearch.org. Just enters the target window in 1867.

---

## Newspapers

- ***Coleraine Chronicle*** (founded 1844): main local paper for the Bushmills/Coleraine area — obituaries, marriage notices, local notices.
- **British Newspaper Archive** (subscription): https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/
- PRONI and local libraries hold microfilm copies.

---

## Repository Summary

| Repository | What it holds | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch.org** | 4 Billy volumes: Presbyterian christenings 1837–1868 & marriages 1837–1864 (full-text searchable); school register 1867–1933; Griffith's valuation Ballylinny (browse-only) | Free |
| **PRONI, Belfast** (2 Titanic Boulevard, BT3 9HQ; proni@communities-ni.gov.uk) | Microfilm of all surviving church registers; Tithe Applotment Books; estate papers; post-1858 probate; yeomanry lists | In-person / by request |
| **RCB Library, Dublin** (Braemor Park, Dublin 14 D14 N735; library@ireland.anglican.org) | Church of Ireland originals and copies not destroyed in 1922 | Subscription search / in-person |
| **NLI Catholic Registers** | Digitised Catholic parish registers | Free — https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| **National Archives of Ireland** (Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85) | Civil registration copies; surviving census fragments; Tithe Applotment Books | In-person / https://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| **Ancestry** | Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915; Marriage License Bonds index; Irish Records Index | Subscription |
| **FindMyPast** | Non-Conformist collections; Ffolliott CoI; Betham/Thrift abstracts | Subscription |
| **RootsIreland** | Indexed Ulster church records | Subscription — http://www.rootsireland.ie/ |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** | Indexed County Antrim records | Subscription — http://www.ancestryireland.com/ |
| **AskAboutIreland / IrishGenealogy.ie** | Griffith's Valuation fully indexed | Free — http://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ |
| **British Newspaper Archive** | *Coleraine Chronicle* from 1844 and Ulster papers | Subscription — https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ |
| **FindAGrave** | Headstone transcriptions | Free — https://www.findagrave.com/ |

---

## Key Record Losses

1. **Two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers** were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. Whether Billy's specific registers were among those deposited (and thus destroyed) or survived elsewhere is unconfirmed — check PRONI's Guide to Church Records first.
2. **Irish census records 1821–1861** were destroyed in the same fire (1861 and 1871 originals destroyed earlier). Use Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books as substitutes.
3. **Pre-1858 probate records** proved in Irish ecclesiastical courts were destroyed in 1922. Only indexes and abstracts survive.

---

## Critical Research Tips

- **Always search under "Coleraine" for Catholic records**, not "Billy." The Billy civil parish is in the RC district of Coleraine, Diocese of Connor, in every index, microfilm catalogue, and online database.
- **The 1780–1836 window lacks confirmed register coverage of any denomination.** For this sub-period, Tithe Applotment Books and estate papers at PRONI are the primary sources.
- **FamilySearch's Billy volumes are full-text searchable but not name-indexed** — use the full-text search function; a standard name-index search will not find entries in them.
- **Check the PRONI Guide to Church Records before anything else** to identify which registers for Billy area churches survive and in what form: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** Ancient ecclesiastical and civil parish; formerly the head of an ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. The rectory and vicarage of Billy alone now constitute the corps of the archdeaconry of Connor. Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Post town / administrative center:** Bushmills; also contains a portion of Dunserverick.
- **Baronies:** Partly in the barony of Carey, chiefly in that of Lower Dunluce.
- **Poor law union:** Coleraine.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster, Ireland (pre-1922); Northern Ireland, United Kingdom (from 1922, after the target period closes).
- **Population during period:** Population data could not be retrieved for this specific parish; no results were returned by the population tool.
- **Religious denominations present:** Church of Ireland (archdeaconry church); Presbyterian (meeting houses); Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterian meeting house); Wesleyan Methodists (meeting house). Roman Catholic population is recorded as part of the district of Coleraine for RC purposes.

## Boundary and jurisdictional notes

- Billy civil parish lies within County Antrim throughout the entire 1780–1870 period; no boundary change affects county-level record jurisdiction.
- For Roman Catholic records, Billy parish falls under the **district of Coleraine** in the Diocese of Connor. Catholic vital-events records for Billy residents will therefore be found in Coleraine parish registers, not in registers labelled "Billy."
- For Church of Ireland records, Billy was the head church of an ecclesiastical union. Surrounding parishes (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) were formerly part of the same union; neighbouring parishes should be checked if Billy registers are missing or destroyed.
- After 1922 the parish fell within Northern Ireland; records for the post-1922 period are administered by PRONI and GRONI in Belfast rather than the Dublin repositories.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Births and deaths:** State-level (Ireland-wide) civil registration began in **1864**. No civil registration exists for births or deaths before that year anywhere in Ireland.
- **Marriages:** State-level registration of **Protestant marriages** began in **1845**; registration of **all marriages** (including Catholic) began in **1864**.
- Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Where held:** General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Belfast, holds civil registration records for County Antrim from these dates. The General Register Office of Ireland, Dublin, also holds copies of all pre-partition records.
- **Gaps:** The entire period **1780–1863** has no civil registration for births or deaths. The period **1780–1844** has no civil registration for any marriages. For the first 86 years of the target window, church registers are the only official source of vital events.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial registers (see Church records section).

### Church records

This section is the most critical for 1780–1870 research in Billy parish because civil registration covers only the final six years of the target window.

**Note on 1922 record loss:** The Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin was destroyed by fire in 1922. Two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers that had been deposited there were lost. For County Antrim parishes, registers that had not yet been sent to Dublin and those held at local churches or PRONI survived. Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)

#### Church of Ireland

- Billy parish was the head of the archdeaconry of Connor. No specific start dates for Billy's own Church of Ireland registers were returned by any tool in this survey.
- Surviving CoI registers for County Antrim parishes are held at:
  - **PRONI** (microfilm copies): 2 Titanic Boulevard, Titanic Quarter, Belfast, BT3 9HQ, Northern Ireland. Tel: 028 9053 4800. Email: proni@communities-ni.gov.uk. PRONI's Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) identifies which Billy-area registers survive and whether they are on microfilm or in original form at PRONI.
  - **Representative Church Body (RCB) Library** (Church of Ireland, holds surviving originals and transcripts): Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735, Ireland. Tel: +353 (0)1 492 3979. Email: library@ireland.anglican.org. Request a search: https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy. Full list of parish registers: https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf
- **Online indexes for CoI records:**
  - [Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239) at FamilySearch — index and images, free. Connor diocese bonds are included.
  - [Irish Parish Register Baptisms & Confirmations, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Irish Parish Register Marriages, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-marriages-ffolliott-collection) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Irish Parish Register Burials, Ffolliott Collection](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/irish-parish-register-burials-ffolliott-collection) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Betham Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — abstracts of records including pre-1922 CoI material; a useful substitute for destroyed originals (subscription).
  - [Thrift Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — includes wills, parish registers, pedigree charts back to the 16th century (subscription).
- **Gap:** Pre-1922 register dates for Billy CoI are unconfirmed by this survey. The gap in the 1780–1837 period is especially acute. If the registers were held locally or at PRONI when the 1922 fire occurred, they may survive; check PRONI's Guide to Church Records (URL above) first.

#### Roman Catholic

- Billy civil parish falls within the **RC district of Coleraine**, Diocese of Connor. Catholic registers for Billy residents will be labelled under Coleraine, not Billy. No specific start date for Coleraine's Catholic registers was returned by this survey.
- The [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) states that most rural Irish Catholic parishes did not begin keeping registers until Catholic Emancipation in 1828–1829. Pre-1829 Catholic records for rural County Antrim are very sparse.
- **Online access to Catholic registers:**
  - [Catholic Records, National Library of Ireland](https://registers.nli.ie/) — free; the NLI holds a large digitised collection of Irish Catholic parish registers.
  - [Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/) at Ancestry — index and images (subscription).
  - [Ireland Roman Catholic Parish Marriages](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-roman-catholic-parish-marriages) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [RootsIreland](http://www.rootsireland.ie/) — indexed database of Irish church records including Catholic registers, subscription.
  - [Ulster Historical Foundation](http://www.ancestryireland.com/) — has indexed Catholic records for some Ulster parishes, subscription.
- **Physical custody of originals:** PRONI holds microfilm copies of many County Antrim Catholic registers. The original Coleraine registers are held at the local parish.
- **Gap for 1780–1828:** No Catholic registers for Billy/Coleraine district are likely to survive for this sub-period. Substitute sources for Catholic families in this window include Tithe Applotment Books (1820s), Griffith's Valuation (1848–1864), and any surviving estate records.

#### Presbyterian

- Billy civil parish contains Presbyterian meeting houses (congregation(s) in Bushmills area) and a Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian) meeting house. Source: [Billy Civil Parish wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **FamilySearch digitised volumes confirmed for Billy parish (townland of Ballylinny within Billy):**
  - **Christenings, 1837–1868** (image group 007907410_008_M9VF-SK5): 65 images; full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed — must be searched by text, not browsed by name. Access at FamilySearch.org.
  - **Marriage Records, 1837–1864** (image group 007765074_009_M9VX-Q7W): 50 images; full-text searchable but NOT name-indexed. Access at FamilySearch.org.
- **Physical custody:** Originals are in the custody of the local congregation. Microfilm copies are held at **PRONI** (Belfast). The [Ireland Church Records wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) confirms that the average start date for Presbyterian registers in Northern Ireland is around 1830, consistent with the 1837 start of these volumes.
- **Online access to non-conformist registers:**
  - [Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Ireland, Non-Conformist Marriages](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Ireland, Non-Conformist Burials](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
  - [Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) at FindMyPast — index (subscription).
- **Gap for 1780–1836:** No Presbyterian register start dates before 1837 are confirmed for Billy parish by any tool in this survey. The period 1780–1836 is unconfirmed for Presbyterian records.

#### Wesleyan Methodist and Covenanter (Reformed Presbyterian)

- Both denominations had meeting houses in Billy parish. No specific register information was returned by any tool for either denomination in this parish.
- **PRONI Guide to Church Records** (URL above under Church of Ireland) identifies what Methodist and Covenanter registers survive for the Billy area.
- **Online access:** FindMyPast non-conformist collections (links above under Presbyterian) cover Methodist and other nonconformist bodies. [Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) may include Covenanter session records.
- **Language of records:** English throughout.

### Census records

- **Irish census:** A census was taken in Ireland in 1821, 1831, 1841, 1851, 1861, 1871 (1871 falls just outside the target window's end). The 1821–1851 census records for County Antrim were largely destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire. Some fragments and abstracts survive; check PRONI.
- **1901 and 1911 census:** Fully surviving and online at the National Archives of Ireland (https://www.nationalarchives.ie/), but these fall after the target period.
- **Substitute enumerations:** Griffith's Valuation (1848–1864) and Tithe Applotment Books (1820s) function as census substitutes for the target period (see Tax records below).
- **FamilySearch Catalog search was not run in this survey;** additional digitised census fragments may be held in the FamilySearch Catalog under County Antrim or Billy.

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills, letters of administration, estate inventories.
- **Irish jurisdiction:** The Prerogative Court of Armagh had jurisdiction over larger estates; the Consistorial Court of Connor had jurisdiction over probate in County Antrim. All pre-1858 wills proved in Irish ecclesiastical courts were destroyed in 1922.
- **Post-1858:** The Principal Registry and district registries took over probate from 1858. These records are held at PRONI for County Antrim.
- **Online index (pre-1858 wills, destroyed originals):**
  - [Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62077/) at Ancestry — index (subscription). These are indexes to records destroyed in 1922.
  - [Thrift Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — includes will abstracts (subscription).
  - [Betham Genealogical Abstracts](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts) at FindMyPast — includes genealogical abstracts from pre-1922 wills (subscription).
- **Physical:** PRONI holds post-1858 County Antrim probate calendars and wills.
- The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland Probate Records returned only generic content in this survey; consult PRONI directly for County Antrim probate guidance.

### Land records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s):** Tithe payments were recorded parish by parish beginning in the 1820s. These name the occupiers of land (not tenants or labourers without land). A key pre-census substitute. Source: [Billy Civil Parish wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1848–1864):** Richard Griffith's property valuation names occupiers of land and houses by townland. FamilySearch has a digitised (browse-only) volume for the townland of Ballylinny within Billy parish:
  - **VAL 12B/1/7B, Ballylinny, Billy, 1867–1881** (image group 004689599): 76 images, NOT name-indexed, NOT full-text searchable — must be browsed image by image.
- **Deeds:** The Registry of Deeds, Dublin, records land transactions from 1708. County Antrim deeds from the target period should be searchable there.
- **Estate papers:** Many County Antrim families were tenants of large estates. Estate papers (leases, rent rolls) can be very detailed; PRONI holds major collections.
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds.
- The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland Land and Property returned only generic content in this survey.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** Rebellion of 1798 (United Irishmen), Napoleonic Wars (British Army service), and later 19th-century British Army service.
- **Record types:** British Army service and pension records; militia muster rolls; yeomanry lists. County Antrim had active yeomanry units in the 1798 period.
- **Where held:** The National Archives (UK), Kew, London, holds British Army service records. PRONI holds some militia and yeomanry records for Ulster.
- No military volumes were returned by FamilySearch volume_search for Billy parish in this period.

### Cemetery records

- **Denominations:** Cemeteries associated with the Presbyterian meeting house and the Church of Ireland are the most likely repositories.
- **Online coverage:** [FindAGrave](https://www.findagrave.com/) — free; check for Billy area headstone transcriptions.
- **Sexton records:** No sexton records for Billy were returned by this survey; check PRONI.

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The *Coleraine Chronicle* (founded 1844) is the main local paper for the Coleraine/Bushmills area during the target period and would carry obituaries, marriage notices, and local notices.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) holds digitised runs of many Ulster papers (subscription). PRONI and local libraries hold microfilm copies.

### Immigration and emigration records

- Significant emigration from County Antrim occurred throughout the 1780–1870 period, particularly to North America. Presbyterian families were among the heaviest emigrants (the "Scots-Irish" stream).
- **Relevant ports:** Larne, Belfast, and Londonderry/Derry were the main Ulster ports of departure. Liverpool was also widely used.
- **Record types:** Passenger lists, US naturalization records, and Canadian land grants. No passenger volumes for Billy were returned by FamilySearch volume_search.
- **Online:** [Ireland Emigration and Immigration wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Emigration_and_Immigration); passenger lists indexed on Ancestry and FamilySearch for the receiving ports.

### Tax records

- **Tithe Applotment Books (1820s):** Names landholders by townland; held at PRONI and partially digitised at the National Archives of Ireland website and Ancestry.
- **Griffith's Valuation (1848–1864):** Names all property occupiers by townland. The FamilySearch browse-only volume VAL 12B/1/7B covers Ballylinny within Billy (image group 004689599, 76 images). Griffith's is fully indexed and searchable free at [AskAboutIreland.ie](http://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/) and also at [IrishGenealogy.ie](https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/).
- **Substitute value for census loss:** Because most pre-1861 census records for County Antrim were destroyed in 1922, Tithe Applotment Books and Griffith's Valuation are the primary substitutes for locating families in the 1820–1864 window.

### School records

- **Deffrick National School Girls' Register** (image group 008682995_005_M94W-68Y): 50 images, covering April 1867 – September 1933. Browse-only; NOT name-indexed, NOT full-text searchable. The register just enters the target window in 1867.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840s–1860s)

## Jurisdiction Overview
- **Formed:** 1811
- **County seat:** Pottsville
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States

> **Note:** FamilySearch Wiki pages for Pennsylvania and Schuylkill County returned only generic content during this survey. Consult the wiki directly at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/ for Pennsylvania-specific registration dates, naming customs, and additional strategies.

---

## Available Record Types

### ✅ Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- Pennsylvania did **not** have statewide civil registration in the 1840s–1860s. No digitized civil vital records were confirmed for this county and period.
- **Primary alternative:** Church records (see below) are the go-to source for births, marriages, and deaths in this era.

---

### ✅ Church Records
- **Volume 004288771** — Lutheran Church Records, Schuylkill County, 1840–1875. 198 images.
  - **Browse-only** (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable) — must be browsed page by page.
  - Languages: **English and German** — German-language entries require a reader.
- One additional synthetic/test-fixture collection was returned; treat with caution and verify at FamilySearch before relying on it.
- Other denominations active in this period are **not confirmed** as digitized.

---

### ✅ Census Records (Best Online Access)
- **Volume 007621224** — U.S. Federal Census, Schuylkill County, 1850–1860. 412 images. **96% name-indexed, full-text searchable** — the best-access record confirmed for this period.
- Also available on **Ancestry**: 1850 United States Federal Census — https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/
- No state census or mortality schedule volumes were confirmed for this period.

---

### ✅ Probate Records
- **Collection 1999196** — Pennsylvania Probate Records, 1683–1994. 3.2 million images, **browse-only** (0 name-indexed records).
- **Volume 004812990** — Probate Records, Schuylkill County, 1845–1880. 286 images. **Full-text searchable** but only 4% name-indexed.
  - Important: A negative name search does not confirm absence — browse the volume as well.
- Covers both testate (wills) and intestate (administrations) estates.

---

### ⚠️ Land Records
- **Not confirmed online** for this county and period.
- Deed books would be held at the Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds, Pottsville.
- Pennsylvania uses **metes and bounds** surveying.
- The only Ancestry land record link returned covers Tax & Exoneration Lists 1768–1801 — predates the target period.

---

### ⚠️ Military Records
- Relevant conflicts: **Mexican-American War (1846–1848)** and **Civil War (1861–1865)**.
- No Schuylkill County–specific military volumes or collections were confirmed online.
- Federal records are held at **NARA**; verify via FamilySearch's military collections.

---

### ⚠️ Immigration & Naturalization
- Nearest major port of entry: **Philadelphia**.
- Pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any court of record — search the **Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas**.
- No county-specific volumes confirmed online; check NARA for passenger lists.

---

### ⚠️ Tax Records
- 1840s–1860s tax lists not confirmed as digitized.
- Good substitute for missing census years — verify holdings at county level and Pennsylvania State Archives.

---

### ⚠️ Cemetery, Newspaper & Other Records
- Not confirmed online for this county and period.
- Obituaries, marriage notices, and sheriff's sale notices in 19th-century newspapers can substitute for missing vital records — check Chronicling America and local newspaper archives.

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What's Confirmed | Access |
|---|---|---|
| **FamilySearch** | Federal census (indexed), probate records (partial FT search), Lutheran church records (browse-only) | Free |
| **Ancestry** | 1850 federal census | Subscription |
| **Schuylkill County Courthouse, Pottsville** | Deed books, court records, naturalizations | In-person or mail |
| **Pennsylvania State Archives, Harrisburg** | State-level records, county microfilm | In-person or online request |
| **Schuylkill County Historical Society** | Local histories, cemetery transcriptions, newspapers | Contact for access |

---

## Records NOT Online (Confirmed Gap)
- Civil vital records (births, marriages, deaths)
- Land/deed records
- Tax lists (1840s–1860s)
- Military records
- Cemetery/sexton records
- Newspapers
- Naturalization petitions
- School and institutional records

---

## Research Tips
1. **Start with the federal census** — the 1850 and 1860 censuses are name-indexed and the easiest online entry point.
2. **Lutheran church records** (Vol. 004288771) are browse-only and may be in German — budget time for page-by-page review.
3. **Probate records** are full-text searchable but only 4% indexed — run a full-text search *and* browse the volume.
4. **Pre-1906 naturalizations** may appear in county deed books or Court of Common Pleas minutes — check both.
5. **FamilySearch Wiki** pages for this county returned only generic content in this survey — consult the wiki directly before concluding any record type is unavailable.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840–1880)

*Note: The request named three counties — Pulaski, Greenup, and Boyd. Per survey scope, only Pulaski County is covered here. Greenup and Boyd counties each require a separate locality survey.*

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat:** Somerset
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky, United States
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by survey tools for Pulaski County; the county is in south-central Kentucky
- **Economy:** Primarily subsistence agriculture; timber; the county had no major industrial base during this period
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly native-born American settlers of Scots-Irish and English descent; small enslaved African American population through 1865
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian — the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Key historical events:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state with soldiers serving both Union and Confederate forces; courthouse disasters in 1838 and 1871 destroyed portions of the county record base

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County was established December 10, 1798, from Lincoln and Green counties; boundaries were stable through the target period — no subdivision or annexation was identified by survey tools
- Pre-formation records (before December 10, 1798) are filed under Lincoln County and Green County — both should be searched for events and land transactions preceding county formation

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates:** County-level birth and death registration: 1853–1862, then 1874–1878 (both windows overlap the target period); county-level marriage registration: from county formation (1799 for Pulaski County); statewide birth and death registration: 1911, with general compliance by 1917 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- **What exists:** Marriage bonds and consent forms from 1799; scattered birth and death records within the two county-level registration windows; FamilySearch holds marriage bonds (1799–1871) digitized
- **Where held:** County-level records: Pulaski County Courthouse (100 N. Main Street, #208, Somerset, KY 42502) and KDLA microfilm; statewide records (from 1911): Kentucky Department of Public Health, Office of Vital Statistics
- **Gaps:** No statewide birth or death requirement during 1840–1880; compliance with the county-level system was minimal; the 1871 courthouse disaster destroyed records covering the period immediately before 1871; no county-level birth or death registration 1863–1873 (gap between the two periods)
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (baptisms, marriages, burials); family bibles; tax lists; census mortality schedules; cemetery inscriptions

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian — the dominant groups in Kentucky before 1900
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership lists, church minutes
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Historical Society (described as holding the most comprehensive collection of church records for the county); FamilySearch Library (microfilmed Kentucky church records); Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort); individual denominational archives; some active congregations still hold their own records
- **Online:** FamilySearch — "Kentucky Church Records, 1818–1995" (index and images, described as incomplete); "Kentucky Births and Christenings, 1839–1960" (index only); "Kentucky Marriages, 1785–1979" (index only); "Kentucky Deaths and Burials, 1843–1970" (index only) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records)
- **Gaps:** No tool result confirmed which specific congregation(s) served Pulaski County residents in 1840–1880 — parish affiliation for a given family is unconfirmed. Contact the Pulaski County Historical Society or search the FamilySearch Catalog directly at FamilySearch.org before assuming a denomination
- **Language:** English

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Kentucky counties appear in the federal census from 1810; for the target period: 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 enumerations all cover Pulaski County; the 1890 federal census is largely destroyed nationally
- **State census:** No Kentucky state censuses were taken (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy)
- **Other enumerations:** Mortality schedules accompany the 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 censuses (listing deaths in the preceding year); agricultural and slave schedules provide additional context
- **Access:** Federal census records are indexed and available at Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/census/) and FamilySearch

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations and inventories, guardianships, court orders, civil and criminal cases
- **Date range:** Probate from 1801; court records from 1799
- **Online:** FamilySearch — Pulaski County early will books (1801–1929) have been digitized (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Pulaski_County,_Kentucky_Genealogy)
- **Where held:** Pulaski County Courthouse (originals); KDLA (microfilm copies)
- **Gaps:** The 1838 and 1871 courthouse disasters destroyed portions of the probate and court record base; records covering the years immediately before those dates may be missing or incomplete

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state, not a federal land state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Virginia issued grants for Kentucky territory before 1792; after 1792, Kentucky issued its own grants through the Kentucky Land Office in Frankfort. Grant series relevant to 1840–1880 include the Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856) and Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873) (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Types:** Land grants, patents, warrants, surveys; county deed books (person-to-person transfers from 1799); tax records
- **Online:** FamilySearch — Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants, and related records (1700–1955), digitized images; Ancestry — Kentucky land grants and related records (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- **Where held (originals):** Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort (grants, patents, warrants, surveys); Pulaski County Courthouse (deed books from 1799)

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848); Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky soldiers served both Union and Confederate forces
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants (at NARA); Kentucky state adjutant general records (at KDLA); draft registrations
- **Where held:** NARA (https://www.archives.gov/); Fold3 (https://www.fold3.com/) for digitized service and pension records; KDLA for state-level military records

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) — search Pulaski County for indexed burials and memorial photos
- **Physical records:** Individual church and community cemeteries; the Pulaski County Historical Society maintains records and obituaries from local newspapers that document burials

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** This survey did not confirm specific Pulaski County newspaper titles or their date ranges from tool results

Here is the locality guide for Alabama around 1800:

---

**Locality Guide — Alabama Region, circa 1800 (Pre-Statehood)**

The Alabama region around 1800 was **not yet a state**. It passed through at least three distinct jurisdictional layers a researcher must follow:

1. **Spanish Colonial (Mobile area until 1813)** — Spanish-period church registers, census returns, and land grants survive in the **Archivo General de Indias** in Seville, Spain, with copies held at the **Library of Congress**.

2. **Mississippi Territory (1798–1817)** — The Alabama portion of the territory was administered from Natchez. Key records include:
   - **Territorial censuses of 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810** — held in person at the **Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH)** in Montgomery; not currently available online.
   - **Territorial court and land records, 1799–1820** — digitized on FamilySearch as browse-only (unindexed) volumes; must be read page by page.

3. **Early Alabama Counties** — County formation dates matter. No indexed FamilySearch collections open until 1803 (church records), 1809 (marriages and probate), so events right at 1800 fall in a coverage gap.

**Key repositories to consult:**
- **Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH)**, Montgomery — the primary state repository for territorial-era records.
- **FamilySearch** — browse-only digitized territorial court and land volumes; some indexed collections starting 1803+.
- **Archivo General de Indias**, Seville (with Library of Congress copies) — for the Mobile area under Spanish rule.

**Recommended next step:** Narrow your ancestor's location to a specific county or area within Alabama. The county's formation date and what records survive locally will determine exactly where to search first.
